claim_reviews.conclusion: The cue “fish sauce” and the sense “salty sauce made from fermented fish” are aligned and materially accurate.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Kecap ikan” is an established Indonesian term for fish sauce.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: kecap ikan

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Sos ikan” is an established Malaysian Malay term for fish sauce.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: sos ikan

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” correctly indicates distinct national forms with the same sense; the Indonesian alternative “saus ikan” does not invalidate the selected answer.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false-friend error affects the card. A useful contrast is that Malaysian “kicap” normally denotes soy sauce, whereas “sos ikan” denotes fish sauce.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both answers correctly express “fish sauce” for the stated salty, fermented-fish sauce sense. Indonesian “kecap ikan” and Malaysian “sos ikan” are established national terminology preferences, so “different-common-word” is appropriate. No learner-critical false-friend error is present; Malaysian “kicap” generally refers to soy sauce, not the fish-sauce answer given here.
